page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is equipped with 4 vCPUs running on 2 physical Intel Xeon 8559C cores at 3.2 GHz, supporting hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. System RAM consists of 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM allocation per core. Local storage is provided through a bundled 2,500 GB NVMe SSD. Networking capabilities include a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. The underlying processor includes vector and matrix acceleration flags, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU execution alongside balanced overall system operations. In Geekbench single-core tests, the instance scored 2314.0, accompanied by single-threaded gzip compression performance of 34.74 GB/sec. Multi-core performance metrics are lower, with stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and software compilation benchmarking returning lower percentile rankings. Memory access bandwidth shows lower read speeds during large uncached operations at 34.18 GB/sec, contrasted with average write speeds at 36.32 GB/sec. Benchmark tasks for Redis SET operations reached 6.09 million operations per second, while static web serving recorded 8.21 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost efficiency perspective, the high ratio of local NVMe SSD capacity to core count offers high resource density for IO-heavy workloads without needing discrete hardware accelerators. The instance exhibits tradeoffs where single-threaded execution is prioritized over heavy multi-threaded processing efficiency. Suitable workloads include database operations, key-value caches, text processing applications, and local disk-bound server deployments.
